home.ct_p: Questions, ideas, a library that wants to join the network or a Z39.50 server worth adding to the list: write here and the answer reaches your e-mail.
home.ct_name_ph: Your name or the library's name
home.ct_msg_ph: Send your suggestion, constructive criticism, problem report, a new library server to add, or a question about Koha-Nexus...
home.ct_ok: Message sent! Thank you for getting in touch.
home.ct_err: The message could not be sent right now. Check the fields and try again in a moment.
home.ct_note: Your e-mail is only used to answer this message.
home.p_h2: One screen for every task, with mouse and keyboard.
home.p_p: Run sudo config.sh and the panel opens full screen: a live dashboard, cards you click, shortcut keys and a command palette (ctrl+p). These are real screenshots of the panel.
home.pd_dashboard: Koha's state, the last backup, free disk and every address of the catalog and the staff interface (this computer, the local network and the internet), each with Open and Copy buttons.
home.pd_hub: E-mail, WhatsApp & Telegram, SMS, SIP2 and Z39.50 on one screen. Links open the exact Koha staff page, a Gmail cheat sheet fills the SMTP form, and a SIP2 form writes SIPconfig.xml for the self-check machine.
home.pd_z3950: Public catalogues by region plus a community list. The scan runs a real search on each server and keeps only those that return a valid MARC record, ranked by speed.
home.pd_opac: The public catalogue's look in one click: frosted glass or brushed metal, rounded corners, a wallpaper, logo, a light/dark switch and a New arrivals carousel with real covers. A backup is taken first.
home.pd_vpn: A private WireGuard network for the staff: add a phone or laptop, scan its QR code, and the staff interface and SSH work from anywhere. Split tunnel only: the device's own internet is untouched.
home.pd_crons: Every scheduled job with a switch, how often and the time, instead of a text editor. Lines written by hand are kept and the old file is saved first.
home.pd_ai: AI cataloguing from photos of the cover and title page, and an assistant on Koha's staff home page that answers in plain language and changes data only after Approve & Execute.
home.pd_backup: Restoring the database now lives only here, next to the MARC21 export and the backup routines: the main menu no longer has a separate Restore database option. Download the latest backup to this PC, restore the database from a backup (tested first, with a safety copy of the current one), export the MARC21 records with one button, test a backup in a temporary database and copy it to Google Drive, OneDrive, MEGA or S3, step by step.
home.f12_d: Curated public catalogues tested with a real search: only servers that return valid MARC records go into Koha, fastest first.
home.f13_d: Textures, rounded corners, wallpaper, logo, a light/dark switch and a New arrivals carousel, written into Koha with a backup first.
home.f14_d: E-mail, SMS, SIP2 self-check and Z39.50 on one screen, with links to the exact Koha page and a SIP2 form that writes the configuration.
home.f15_d: Switch each automated job on or off and choose how often and when. Hand-written lines are kept.
home.f16_d: Staff reach the staff interface and SSH from anywhere with a QR code for their phone. Only the library's addresses go through the VPN.
home.f17_d: A public catalog address on koha.nexus without buying a domain or opening a Cloudflare account, shared as a QR code or a link. Still in testing.
home.f18_d: Librarians ask in plain language about books, patrons and loans. Any change is a proposal that runs only after Approve & Execute.
home.n_live: Live list from the koha.nexus network
home.n_all: See the full list of catalogs
home.hero_h1: The best free library system, now without the hassle.
home.hero_p: koha.nexus is a smart, free, and easy-to-use assistant for installing, configuring, maintaining, and extending the Koha Integrated Library System via a friendly and guided dashboard.
home.feat_h2: A dashboard built for those who keep the library running.
home.feat_p: From the initial installation to backups, indexing, security, migration, cataloging, and web publishing, the core features are gathered in a single control point.
home.f1_d: System, disk, network, and port pre-validation; installation and tuning of Koha, MariaDB, Apache, Memcached, and Plack, plus SWAP, NTP, and timezone.
home.f2_d: Compressed SQL backups, MARC21 exports, a restore test, and cloud copies on Google Drive, OneDrive, MEGA or S3, set up step by step.
home.f3_d: Backups are validated and tested in a temporary database before any replacement of the current catalog.
home.f4_d: Switch between Zebra and Elasticsearch 7, indexer watchdog, and tools for index repair and rebuild.
home.f5_d: Cloudflare Tunnel without needing to open router ports, Certbot for SSL, and Google Search Console assistant.
home.f6_d: Fail2ban, UFW firewall, options to restrict staff access on port 8080, and database password rotation.
home.f7_d: Data import, SQL reports, catalog quality checks, GDPR/LGPD privacy tools, annual patron category rollover, and more.
home.f8_d: Delivery of Koha notices through WhatsApp gateways or a Telegram bot, completely optional.
home.f9_d: PHA or Cutter-Sanborn, DDC, Cutter calculator, safe MARC record replacement, and AI assistance.
home.f10_d: Run Koha on a single Windows PC, complete with desktop shortcuts, notifications, system tray, and diagnostic tools.
home.f11_d: Dashboard updates straight from GitHub with SHA-256 installer verification.
home.inst_h2: Linux installation in a few commands.
home.inst_p: The project targets Debian 11/12/13 or Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 on amd64 or arm64 architecture, and can also run on Windows via WSL 2.
home.inst_b1_d: Download the current installer script and run it with administrative privileges.
home.inst_b2_d: You can also keep translation files alongside the script to work offline.
home.inst_r2: 4 GB of RAM; 8 GB or more recommended
home.inst_r3: 5 GB free space; 10 GB or more recommended
home.inst_r4: root or user with sudo privileges
home.inst_a3: Create your super librarian via the dashboard
home.inst_a5: Reopen the dashboard anytime with sudo config.sh
home.win_h2: A full Koha environment on a single PC, using WSL 2.
home.win_p: The Windows edition is designed for small libraries, training, and evaluation, keeping Koha services inside Debian on WSL 2 while offering native Windows tools.
home.win_d_p: Open PowerShell as Administrator, paste this command and press Enter.
home.win_b_p: Right-click the Start button and choose Terminal (Admin) or Windows PowerShell (Admin), then click Yes. Paste the command above and press Enter.
home.win_admin: Use your own Windows account. If Windows asks for another person's password, sign in to an administrator account first and run it there: Debian, the shortcuts and the restart step are created for the account that runs the installer.
home.win_c2_p1: Restart your PC and repeatedly press the setup key as soon as the screen turns on:
home.win_c2_p2: Inside the BIOS, find Intel Virtualization Technology (VT-x) or AMD SVM / AMD-V, switch it to Enabled, and press F10 to save.
home.win_c2_p3: Can't access BIOS via keys? In Windows, go to Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup (Restart now) → Troubleshoot → Advanced options → UEFI Firmware Settings.
home.w_t1_d: Verifies a compatible Windows version, 64-bit architecture, memory, free space, and BIOS virtualization.
home.w_t2_d: Installs WSL 2, prepares Debian, and configures the administrative user and systemd.
home.w_t3_d: Installs Koha inside Debian and creates Windows shortcuts, scheduled tasks, and control tools.
home.w_t4_d: Configures access for other computers on the local network and tests ports 80 and 8080.
home.w_t5_d: Start, Stop, Restart, status, diagnostics, index rebuild, and safe shutdown are accessible without opening a console.
home.w_c1_d: Crashes, recoveries, backups, low disk space, and unclean shutdowns trigger native Windows alerts.
home.w_c2_d: Exports logs and useful information for support, securely removing passwords, tokens, and keys.
home.w_c3_d: Koha is shut down in stages before WSL and Windows power off to prevent data corruption.
home.t_h2: More than installing Koha: taking care of the collection.
home.t_p: The dashboard tools utilize Koha's own mechanisms and follow a strict protection flow with locking, previewing, confirmation, and verified backups before any data is altered.
home.t1_d: A single entry point for spreadsheets, MARC files, compressed archives, collections, items, patrons, and circulation data.
home.t2_d: Allows reverting a batch import in a controlled manner, preserving catalog integrity.
home.t3_d: Read-only reports for loans, overdues, acquisitions, missing barcodes, items never borrowed, and lost items.
home.t4_d: Moves patrons between categories using criteria defined by the library, with a dry run before execution.
home.t5_d: Runs catalog inconsistency checks without altering the actual records.
home.t6_d: Anonymizes old borrowing histories and securely deletes expired patrons that meet defined criteria.
home.t_c1: Protection by default: Operations that alter data follow a shared lock with backups, previews, confirmations, and a verified PRE-* copy before making changes.
home.s_h2: Automation without hiding what's going on.
home.s_p: The dashboard centralizes recurring tasks and highlights important points for maintenance, diagnostics, and recovery.
home.s1_r1_2: Compressed SQL backup and optional cloud upload
home.s2_l6: ~/importar — input folder for the Magic Import Tool
home.s3_p: The dashboard gathers status, health checks, Apache logs, deep database maintenance, and ready-to-use reports for support.
home.s4_p: The project includes verification after an unclean reboot, creates a new backup, and updates the index when necessary. On Windows, the safe shutdown routine attempts to stop Koha gracefully before the system shuts down.
home.s_c1: Uninstallation is destructive: The uninstall.sh script permanently removes Koha, databases, local backups, and configurations. Backup your data off-server before using it.
home.n_p: Explore the public catalogs maintained by our partner institutions. Search engines follow these links to automatically discover and index their collections.
home.n_load: Fetching catalogs on the koha.nexus network...
home.c_h2: Built to be used, studied, and improved.
home.c_p: The project includes tests, translations, collaboration tools, and installer checksum verification for automatic updates.
home.c1_p: Bats test suite for backup/restore, indexing, library tools, WSL, and Windows components.
home.c2_p: Versioned dictionaries by language, coverage validation, and automatic rejection of translations missing variables.
home.c3_p: The installer uses SHA-256 to securely validate its own updates.
